title: Introduction to Suno AI music generation
text: Hi, I'm Rohan from Humanitarian's AI. This is the first of three training videos on Suno for Lyrical Literacy volunteers. This one covers a single task, making your first song. You don't need a music background, and you don't need to have used an AI tool before. Work along with me and you'll finish

title: Signing in with Discord for Pro credits
text: With a complete track. Here is the whole idea. You type a sentence describing the song you want. Suno returns a finished track, vocals, melody, instruments, arrangement. It is not stitching together recordings. It generates new audio every time. Everything else in this video is detail on how to write that sentence and where to click. Suno

title: Navigating the Suno workspace
text: Is a generative model trained on a very large catalog of music. In training, it learned the patterns linking words to sound. What makes a track read as folk rather than hip-hop, hopeful rather than tense. Given your description, it predicts audio that fits, a segment at a time.

title: Simple Mode: Style, Mood, and Topic prompts
text: Each segment continuing from the one before it. That is why the same prompt never returns quite the same song twice. First, get signed in. Join the Humanitarian's AI Discord. Your team lead has the invite. Go to suno.com and click sign in. Choose Discord as your

title: Generating, comparing, and downloading MP3s
text: Sign-in method. That is what links your account to the organization's pro plan. Use the same Discord account you joined with. Pro access applies automatically once you are in. This is the workspace. The left sidebar is how you move around it and four items matter today. Home is a feed of recent activity. Explore shows what other people have published, useful for hearing how a description turns into sound. Library holds every track you generate, saved automatically. And create is where you make songs. That is where we are going. The create page has three tabs, simple, advanced, and sounds. Advanced is where you control lyrics and song structure. That is part two. Stay on simple. Three things matter here. The song description box, the instrumental toggle for a track with no vocals, and the create button at the bottom. That

Is the entire interface for your first song. Write your description with three ingredients. Style, what genre or sound, folk, pop, hip-hop. Mood, what the music should feel like, hopeful, playful, calm. Topic, what the song is actually about. Put together, a gentle acoustic folk song warm and hopeful about children discovering the joy of reading. Style, mood, topic. That is a complete description. Click create. Suno generates two versions at once, usually in 30 to 60 seconds. Each generation costs five credits. The pro plan carries 2,500 credits a month, about 500 songs. So, you can afford to iterate rather than trying to get it right on the first attempt. Two cards appear, one per version. Press play and listen to both. They interpret the same description differently, and comparing them tells you what your wording actually did. The three-dot menu on

Each card holds what you can do next, remix, edit, share, and download, each opening its own set of choices. Download then MP3 is how you save the file. To review, sign in at suno.com with Discord. Open create and stay on simple. Describe the song as style, mood, and topic in one sentence. Press create and wait about a minute for two versions. Use the three-dot menu to extend, remix, or download. Five credits a generation against 2,500 a month. That is the first pass. We covered what Suno is doing underneath, how to get signed in, how the workspace is laid out, the three-ingredient description, and how to read the two versions you get back. Part two goes deeper on the description itself, how wording changes the output, and when to move from simple to advanced mode. Rohan Vijayakumar, Humanitarian's AI.
